items.title: Add PC backend selection and capability checks
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:pc-backend-selection -->

Define Windows D3D12/Vulkan/DX11 selection, capability checks, and safe failure fallback.

## Implementation and bounded validation

Source 0.4.19 implements typed requested/actual backend selection with environment/config precedence, D3D12 and Vulkan minimum capability checks, explicit DX11/D3D11 Unsupported handling, and bounded D3D12/Vulkan fallback. Startup cleanup releases partial GPU state before the alternative attempt; dual failure reports both reasons before guest execution. The saved preference is retained separately from the fallback backend.

`LoBackendSelectionTest` passed parse/precedence/invalid-request, capability boundaries, explicit DX11, bounded dual failure, success retention, and 21 staged failure/exception-cleanup cases. On RTX 5080, `LoBackendDeviceTest` created and released the native D3D12/Vulkan device-lifecycle objects under the required capabilities; it did not create a window, start the guest, submit GPU commands, draw, or present. The unique main runtime build (session 64666) exited 0.

DX11/DXBC is recognized for policy and future interface purposes only. DX11 runtime support, an active DX11 device, shader execution, and scene validation are not implemented or claimed.

Evidence: `out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/selection/REPORT.md`, `out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/selection/artifact-identity.json`, `out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/selection/evidence-index.json`.

items.title: Isolate caches by backend and compiler identity
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:backend-cache-isolation -->

Bind cache identity to backend, compiler, options, and variant, with safe incompatible-cache recovery.

## Implementation and bounded validation

Source 0.4.19 adds typed success-cache envelopes containing backend/binary format, translator and loaded compiler/validator identities, options, variant, artifact identity, payload length, and digest. DXIL and reserved SM5 DXBC framing are distinguished; malformed, truncated, renamed, legacy-success, or identity-mismatched files are rejected before device creation. Valid 0.4.17 startup bundles retain their compatible fast path, while mismatched compiler, translator, options, variant, or backend inputs invalidate stale success reuse.

Focused validation passed 91 contract checks, 14 isolated builtin cold/warm checks, 10 persisted restart checks, and 5 framing checks. The isolated cold path made two actual DXC calls (one DXIL and one SPIR-V); warm and restart reuse made zero. The unique main runtime build (session 64666) exited 0.

Reserved DXBC recognition distinguishes container framing only; it is not DX11 compilation, cache execution, or runtime support. DX11 remains a separate Todo.

Evidence: `out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/cache/REPORT.md`, `out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/cache/result.json`, `out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/selection/artifact-identity.json`.

## Sources

- out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/cache/REPORT.md
- out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/cache/result.json
- out/v0.5.0/backend-completion/selection/artifact-identity.json

items.title: Validate backend lifecycle and cache recovery
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:pc-backend-lifecycle-validation -->

验证窗口、重开/重启、cache恢复。

## Scope and completion criteria

- [ ] resize/设置重开/进程重启
- [ ] cold/warm/damagedcache
- [ ] 使用save/settings副本并保留D3D12基线

## Validation and acceptance

items.title: Add independent shader logs and cumulative coverage auditing
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:shader-log-coverage-audit -->

## Historical handoff checkpoint

The retained design joins source/link/submitted-draw coverage into a continuing diagnostic loop. The urgent scope was the split of shader events from runtime summaries; cumulative coverage and all-draw audit remain separate design work.

## Scope and completion criteria

- [x] runtime keeps run/crash/severe-shader summaries while shader-*.jsonl records source/link/compile/TAA events
- [x] Record a conservative per-VS HLSL position-dataflow summary and, before `UnknownShader` returns, independently record guarded camera/viewport/depth evidence in compact schema 2 telemetry
- [ ] Record runtime hash→base VS→fetch/layout fingerprint→family/slot with word-FNV and byte-FNV namespaces
- [ ] Classify cache miss, unknown source, translation failure, missing TAA coverage and expected rejection independently
- [ ] Audit every submitted draw, including unknown VS/PS/pass/frame/map and camera/viewport/depth/jitter/upload state
- [ ] Track first/last/count by shader, pass and reason without collapsing world/skeletal/object differences
- [ ] Quantify bounded background logging loss and overhead
- [x] Retain the current and two newest prior runtime/shader session groups while protecting active/custom paths
- [ ] Accumulate coverage by source/translator/TAA-rule version and explicit denominators
- [x] Include shader snapshot availability with F1 without losing the capture when absent
- [x] Keep the new position evidence observational: schema 2 does not automatically authorize jitter

## Current — 2026-09-10, source 0.5.0

Independent shader JSONL, F1 inclusion, exit flush, custom Unicode paths and session retention passed focused fixtures. A normal earlier candidate exit wrote 15,693 contiguous JSONL records ending with a summary. The new `0.5.0-position-evidence-1` client adds one conservative HLSL position-dataflow analysis per VS and records finite guarded camera/viewport/depth evidence before `UnknownShader` returns. Candidate SHA256 `6feb20923e3632ac00b718950927ee245fb6929c7c3bc95e87e9d13f5cd23937` passed 27 C++ rule checks, a retained corpus that detected four c7 paths without falsely matching five non-c7 paths, and seven Worker checks. The deployed Worker accepts schema 1 and schema 2 requests (both HTTP 200); D1 schema-2 retransmit dedup raised `max_draws` from 44 to 54, and the precise test rows were deleted and read back empty.

A hidden, muted D3D12 RTX 5080 1280×720 experimental-TAA Map16 Main Street run used the unchanged source-0.5.0 executable SHA256 `1beb8a50c5bef1ebf0fb147338b33d558a2193e87f82b0b8c579ecbcb856959d`. Its first periodic receipt collected 23 sources and the second added 32, for 55 programs (15 VS, 40 PS) and 19,188 bytes. Every source matched the real cache byte-for-byte, by SHA256, renderer byte-FNV and length; the final read-only D1 snapshot had 55 sources, 55 associations and no duplicate stage/hash keys, plus 28 matching structured records. Completed-present Map16 windows were 59.67 FPS / 18.036 ms P95 before the second upload and 59.84 FPS / 18.067 ms P95 during it; each had one frame over 50 ms, none over 100 ms and no missing completed frame index. This shows continued rendering during the controlled upload, not an opt-out A/B, general zero-overhead result or full-game performance claim. The task-owned process was stopped; test save/profile, seed and executable remained unchanged.

Cumulative coverage and all-submitted-draw auditing remain In Progress; the unknown 4bd/c230 actual-draw gap remains unvalidated and no jitter authorization was added. The legacy `LO_CAPTURE_REQUEST` is not product F1 capture, so F1 export/source manifest/immediate upload remain pending. Vulkan, AMD, reported visual defects and player acceptance remain pending. The v0.5.2 release provenance is recorded separately in the Project evidence.

## Current extension — 2026-09-10, source 0.5.2

Work has started on bounded, opt-in structured TAA evidence for final texture bindings, producer timing, actual jitter and VS/PS pairing. Collection must remain non-blocking. This extension has no focused validation, package/release or player acceptance evidence yet, and does not authorize a visual repair or a broader TAA claim.

## Private D1 archive — 2026-09-10

The user authorized a daily 03:17 UTC GitHub Action in private `freefrank/LostOdysseyRecomp-build-inputs` to incrementally archive opt-in D1 inputs. The contract uses stage and SHA deduplication, metadata ID deduplication, content addressing, a verified checkpoint that does not advance on failure, and full validation before a checkpoint advances. Its first CI run, [34493751731](https://github.com/freefrank/LostOdysseyRecomp-build-inputs/actions/runs/34493751731), succeeded: 3,401 diagnostics, 431 unique VS/PS sources (77 VS, 354 PS), 909 GPU associations, 31 temporal records and 462 payloads were remotely read back and verified through `2026-09-10T15:07:15Z`. The archived data is at `8da2b10e6a938197f5780f7e61ab6fb6861d1d9f`; the repository remains private and the next scheduled run is 2026-09-11 03:17 UTC.

## Schema 3 implementation and validation — 2026-09-10, source 0.5.2

The bounded local schema-3 queue and Worker contract are implemented. 82 queue checks and 32 producer checks reported zero producer allocations; the seven retained Worker checks and nine new ones passed. A 9,761 B C++ payload with eight records completed three local HTTP-to-Worker-to-SQLite round trips with HTTP 200; replay preserved eight rows and 1,048 leaf fields including 640 IEEE bit fields. The Worker deployment `4db7e156-8a21-4f57-8f0d-bacd0c4576ab` passed health checks 1–3 with request logging still disabled. The local source-0.5.2 client build is 82,904,064 B, SHA256 `c3711463fd4d21f17b68af27cecd2df35851af49e9567e956596b48a7ae1e259`, linked at 2026-09-10T15:12:33Z. It is not a released client package; no game scene, new F1 menu or player acceptance evidence exists. The e810 renderer scope is bounded to at most one invocation per PS per frame and does not claim a mapping repair.

## New shader review — 2026-09-10

The latest read-only D1 checkpoint remains 431 unique programs, 3,401 diagnostics and 31 temporal sequences. Since the 15:07 archive cutoff there are no new programs or diagnostics; 23 GPU associations increased the total from 909 to 932, last seen at 2026-09-10T15:33:41Z. It has 517 schema-1, 2,884 schema-2 and zero schema-3 records, so no new binding runtime evidence exists. `6a8c2c78737dc94c` is a c7 candidate for priority VS review, but its actual VS transform remains unreviewed. For `02d8d17463de32cd` and `3f522a748751d16a`, paired PS code consumes `i4.xy/i4.w` through c0 to sample texture0 RGB; without exact VS review and final texture binding, producer timing and jitter-consistency evidence, i4 cannot be asserted to be clip or target-VP dependent. Schema 3 currently samples only e810 with its two paired PS paths, so it does not cover these two new VS/PS pairs; waiting on the existing client cannot automatically produce their binding evidence. These are diagnostic leads only, not mapping repairs, visual fixes or acceptance.

## Private feedback analysis ledger — 2026-09-10

The private offline ledger provides `sync`, `report` and `review` commands with an exclusive lock, atomic replacement, content-dependency fingerprints and separate manual conclusions. Thirteen new offline fixtures passed once in 0.511 s. The installed skill wrapper imported the existing private archive through cutoff `1789052835` (3,401 observations and 431 sources): its first sync updated 18 cases and its second left all 18 unchanged, with ledger SHA256 `d2176a72cde85d132d725a7cde2f41391d988cafe83843316008ee0962fd9b38` and mtime unchanged. Sixteen historical reviews remain only as unbound history; all 18 cases need review and none has a current manual conclusion. Newly surfaced `32f09dcd84b93237` and `3638b6b020b068fc` are automatic candidates without semantic review. The ledger does not create shader repairs, validation or player acceptance.

## Compact automatic telemetry — started 2026-09-10

Development has started on opt-in compact automatic telemetry intended to reduce reliance on large F1 exports. The authorized scope adds capability, coverage and missing-reason metadata; bounded evidence correlation; final TAA-history diagnostics reused from existing logs; and ledger consumption of structured metadata. Existing opt-in, non-blocking producer and privacy boundaries remain.

## Compact automatic telemetry — local implementation and validation 2026-09-10

The local source-0.5.2 implementation completed a fixed 32-frame CPU window with a 180-second bound, up to 24 pairs and 8 bindings, capped at 32 KiB (actual C++ payload: 18,905 B). It records capability and aggregate observation reasons, pending/upload outcomes, final CPU-history rejection state, relative offsets and server content-SHA correlation. It excludes random, session and device IDs, color images, raw F1 data and new-GPU waits. The retained limitation is that old sparse exact joins are unavailable; sparse support is D3D12-only and binding coverage remains the two e810 pairs.

The new C++ checks (68, zero allocations), Worker checks (9), ledger checks (8) and archive-compatibility check (1) passed. An actual C++ payload completed two loopback HTTP-to-actual-SQLite 200 paths with one deduplicated row preserving fields; that row then passed archive import, installed-skill consumption and an isolated ledger with 32 frames, one pair, eight bindings and nine references. The current archive wrapper left the existing 18 cases and ledger SHA/mtime unchanged. The one local build completed at 2026-09-10T16:42:36Z: 82,946,560 B, SHA256 `59f039ea84404c1ab85095a95a10b32d435bf1d39b1ca610b38d15edb44ce62e`.

Private archive schema-4 compatibility remains pushed at `728d6030980a7be39feca493319f54bfb1a62e74`; Worker deployment `14e74c54-1213-4240-9877-047f35cdda75` remains live with schema 1–4 health checks. v0.5.3 was published as Latest at 2026-09-10T17:18:02Z from `6fa9adc281c5693ac0af8a47fec815b20c29ff50`; CI `34505504344` succeeded in 16m47s. The 44,237,807 B ZIP SHA256 `53beb197b753fa26c5c436f37c4b03bb636857c7390171d3ce6353940a9d81d0` passed 50 payload hash/CRC and clean-provenance checks; its 848,896 B standalone updater SHA256 is `1ad8a0b6e605f050376d59050bf94d598bbd9ec2965610df30cd5e6083fcc5a2`. All four public assets matched audited size/digest with anonymous HEAD 200, and Latest API returned v0.5.3. Publication does not establish a game scene, visual repair, player acceptance or full updater transaction.

- `out/v0.5.0/shader-source-collection/runtime/REPORT.md`
- `out/v0.5.0/shader-source-collection/runtime/D1-VERIFICATION.md`

items.title: Assess and implement DLC import support
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:dlc-import-support -->

支持 Lost Odyssey DLC 与游戏光盘的统一自动识别导入；DLC 格式参考 re:Blue 的 STFS 容器契约。该工作属于 v0.5.0 目标。用户已授权把当前工作树从最后已提交的 source 0.4.2 按功能分批归档；本工作已归入 source 0.4.15 批次并本地提交为 [`f77d943261e14105d17c880ffa40c171b4191dcc`](https://github.com/freefrank/LostOdysseyRecomp/commit/f77d943261e14105d17c880ffa40c171b4191dcc)。该提交已备份到 GitHub `0.5.0`，尚未发布。

## Scope and completion criteria

- [x] 识别 CON/LIVE/PIRS STFS Marketplace 包，Title ID 4D5307FA、原 header 内容标识与来源 SHA256
- [x] DLC 事务导入、取消回滚、重复内容校验与冲突保护；保留原包、存档、profile、配置和缓存
- [x] 共用 game/dlc 内容目录，运行时枚举、异步打开／挂载、读取和关闭
- [x] 移除手动 DLC／Game Discs 模式选择：对多选文件、目录和混合来源按内容自动分类、统一复核并分派导入

## Validation and acceptance

source 0.4.15 统一导入批次已经实现并通过 15/15 项直接受影响检查（13 项新增识别／扫描／复核／分派检查，2 项既有 GUI 检查复用）。未改动的 STFS parser、DLC 交易和运行时读取继续复用先前 22 项 Python 专项检查与两个无窗口／无渲染／无音频的原生模式证据；它们不重复执行。自动导入报告：`out/v0.5.2/auto-import/installer/REPORT.md` 与 `result.json`。

历史 source 0.5.1 本地 DLC ZIP 及 source 0.5.0 候选的名称、SHA256 和保留路径仍是历史产物证据，不代表当前源码编号或公开 Release。用户已提供《失落的奥德赛》实际 DLC 样本，真实验证恢复进行。三包 Folder 首次导入成功；Files 重复导入报告 3 unchanged／0 imported，13 个导出 payload/metadata 文件的 bytes/hash/mtime、原包和测试 game-path 均保持。离线 exact-fault/provenance 诊断修复运行时持久 filter，避免 `spa.bin` 混入 `*.fpi` 枚举；新的 30-call fixture 通过。实际 DLC 奖励、区域与版本兼容性和用户验收仍待补。保持 In Progress / Implemented；已备份到 GitHub `0.5.0`，尚未发布。

items.title: Evaluate frame generation integration
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:frame-generation-research -->

## v0.7.0 frame-generation plan

The planned Windows PC delivery requires 2× DLSS-G and 2× FSR Frame Generation on both D3D12 and Vulkan. Each of the four provider/API combinations has independent acceptance gates; D3D12 diagnosis does not defer Vulkan. This plan does not include FSR Super Resolution or sharpening, DLSS SR, higher multipliers, DX11, Switch, Linux/Steam Deck, or a release date.

P0 fixes SDK, licensing, device, queue and presentation routes. P1 validates the retained native-velocity path and same-frame coverage before fallback work. P2 completes camera, rigid and skeletal motion vectors; P3 freezes color/UI/frame inputs and reset/lifetime rules; P4 establishes both API foundations; P5 and P6 implement FSR FG and DLSS-G on both APIs; P7 accepts the four combinations; P8 prepares a separately authorized release.

This is planning only: implementation, SDK validation, game tests, player acceptance and publication have not started.

Dependencies (source keys): `native-object-motion`, `temporal-color-exposure`, `issue10-fsr-upscaling-frame-generation`.

items.title: Port and validate Linux and Steam Deck
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:linux-steamdeck-platform -->

Linux/Steam Deck remain independent platform work; the bounded Linux first-playable result does not imply native Linux or Steam Deck support.

## First-playable evaluation — implemented and WSL-validated

The 2026-09-13 evaluation remains the planning record. The first-playable target is a Vulkan-only unbundled ELF launched with `./LostOdysseyRecomp --game <disc>` on host Mesa + SDL2 + X11/XWayland, reaching the game screen.

## Scope and completion criteria

- [x] Establish the Linux toolchain, dependencies, Vulkan window/device path, input/audio/file paths and the `--game` launch route for the bounded host path.
- [x] Resolve the first-playable shader compiler/cache identity, PPC compilation, host path/CRT, case-folding and address-space blockers.
- [x] Configure, compile and run the unbundled ELF on WSL2 Manjaro with Mesa Dozen (RTX 5080 through dzn), reaching a 1280x720 Vulkan window.
- [ ] After first playable, separately validate native Linux ICD and real Steam Deck execution, packaging, whole-game flow, controller, save path, resolution and performance.

## Out of scope for this branch's first playable

Installer, F1 debug menu, updater, AppImage, Flatpak, Steam Deck packaging and D3D12-on-Linux.

## Validation and acceptance

The WSL2 Manjaro foreground run on 2026-09-14 around 00:26–00:36 local exited 0 after the user closed the window at about 594 seconds. The ELF was 246294968 bytes with BuildID `bade81073a37e1e262e4c5ec7bef67e80037ee9a`; Vulkan used Mesa Dozen wrapping an RTX 5080 through WSL Vulkan-on-D3D12, the 1280x720 swapchain used the BGRA fallback from RGBA, XEX loaded from `/mnt/d/Mihoyo/LostOdysseyRecomp-windows-x64/game/disc1`, 28482/28484 shaders were ready, and audio was unmuted. This is first-playable WSL evidence only: it is not whole-game acceptance, native Linux ICD validation, Steam Deck validation, a published Linux package, or evidence that the published Windows v0.5.11 ZIP includes Linux.

Source version 0.5.11 is implementation progress on the `linux` branch, not a Linux publication. Remaining work includes native Linux ICD, Steam Deck, packaging, whole-game/controller/save/performance validation.

Dependencies (source keys): `vulkan-runtime-integration`.

items.title: P2: Validate FSR visual quality and multi-platform hardware
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:temporal-phased-p2-fsr-quality-hardware -->

## Summary and objectives

Tune FSR 3.1.4 visual quality across color spaces, transparency masks, and sharpening, and validate across AMD, NVIDIA, native Linux, and Steam Deck hardware.

## Scope and completion criteria

- [ ] Adapt DisplayEncoded SDR color transfer round-trip (decode to linear SDR -> FSR -> re-encode) with grayscale and highlight verification.
- [ ] Generate reactive and transparency masks from verified particle, magic, smoke, and fine-line passes.
- [ ] Establish RCAS sharpening and mip bias policy to prevent over-sharpening or affecting HUD/FMVs.
- [ ] Conduct side-by-side comparison across Off, original TAA, DLSS, and FSR at identical output resolutions.
- [ ] Complete independent hardware validation across AMD and NVIDIA GPUs and native Linux; use the user-accepted APEX 15W Deck proxy for this iteration without claiming Steam Deck hardware equivalence.

## Status and scope

G003/P2 remains In Progress; final visual acceptance is pending. Delivered checkpoint: `ebefab459515fcd629e9758c8726d5b9b6c4b04b`. The manual-run candidate was `cb41c99cdc44456864ac0d44cfcd815c2d099f89595840f4e76df2a2db12c352` (source `d78d80f3add32494c53f67702d27d52c5c5e23aa82d690339cba046768c6357e`); these identify that run, not a current release. Windows FSR Vulkan mask/RCAS and transient-fallback work is delivered with three battle shader mappings. CPU fixture passed 768 samples. GPU fixtures covered the three mapped programs in six DXIL/SPIR-V variants, including Vulkan alpha/depth, palette-motion and QuadList checks. One Windows RTX 5080 Vulkan battle window recorded 2,476 completed FSR uses and zero `mv_first_failure`; this is bounded scene evidence, not full-game coverage or visual acceptance. The user accepted APEX 15W as this iteration's Deck proxy; it is not hardware-equivalent to Steam Deck. SDK consumption and controlled performance checks passed; latest Linux shader/hot-change coverage remains incomplete. `f6` has fixture coverage only. `02d8` is excluded because screen-UV binding is unproven; no runtime blocker has been established. See [current handoff](../notes/fsr-dlss-fg-codex-handoff.zh-CN.md) and [historical evidence](../notes/fsr-dlss-fg-codex-history.zh-CN.md).

## Validation and acceptance

- Fixed scene comparison matrix: stationary camera with moving character, camera pan/rotation, particles, Aim Ring, and combat text.
- Base render time and actual GPU delta measured without frame-rate speculation.
- Multi-platform hardware matrix verified; unverified hardware (such as Intel GPUs) remains unaccepted.

Dependencies (source keys): `temporal-phased-p1-runnable-fsr`, `taa-motion-quality`.

stage_detail: In progress; Windows postprocess mask propagation slice 03 verified (6 draws recorded/published); clear background and inset fixes verified; Linux not verified for this slice; depth invariance, edge raster rules, prefilter branches, SDK binding, and full P2 quality/performance pending; P0 Gate 1 not passed; P1 complete

items.body:
<!-- lo-project:qol-installer-input-layout -->

Recognize supported directory layouts, ISO images, extracted directories and XEX inputs; assess optional MD5/SHA-256 identification and improve the installer UI without weakening compatibility checks.

The user-authorized installer refinement is implemented and validated in a bounded offscreen UI scope: original-game-inspired styling, native custom window chrome, streamlined instructional copy, and UX improvements preserve strict input validation and transactions. Nine direct UI checks and two affected controller checks passed; final normal/narrow renders were inspected. This is not manual foreground GUI acceptance, an installer EXE build, package, commit, or release.

## Validation and limits

Implementation and proportionate source/synthetic desktop validation are complete. The existing 24-test importer suite passed, followed by 2 targeted cancellation/access tests and 3 strict XEX-identity tests. The actual Tk flow copied 15 synthetic source files with matching hashes, preserved source hashes, wrote the task-local game path and reached 100% with the completion dialog. Strict audited XEX identity remains required. Frozen-installer and DPI/package coverage, real retail input, player acceptance and release are pending.

Evidence: `out/v0.5.0/installer/REPORT.md`, `out/v0.5.0/installer/ui-gate-result.json`.

## v0.5.3 drag-crash regression

On 2026-09-10, the user reported that the released v0.5.3 installer stuttered and then exited while being dragged. Four local Windows events identify ucrtbase 0xc0000409. Dump 41648 traces Tk binding through ctypes SendMessageW, Python WNDPROC and CallWindowProcW into Tk re-entry, ending in PyEval_RestoreThread fatal: GIL released/current thread state NULL.

The local unpublished repair changes custom-chrome drag dispatch from SendMessageW to PostMessageW and supplies screen coordinates. The new message-only HWND DragDispatch case in `python -B tools/tests/test_installer_ui.py` passed 1/1. The same legacy UI fixture failed twice in setup on its unchanged foreground assertion, before reaching the changed drag behavior; this is neither positive nor negative evidence for the repair.

The installer-only replacement EXE was built locally as `out/installer-drag-fix/dist/InstallGame.exe` (11,888,743 bytes, SHA-256 `707CD7D2E9F4AB3BF33363E172FAAD5CFCFA6B1A53161FEE0E7F53735B7C7FA7`). A read-only embedded-PYZ inspection confirms PostMessageW drag dispatch and required modules. The user accepted the repair as resolved on 2026-09-10, establishing the reported drag path; the repair remains unpublished.

items.body:
<!-- lo-project:qol-shader-cache-startup-diagnosis -->

Investigate and repair the reported repeated shader-cache compilation at every launch: measure actual cache hits and recompilation causes, reuse valid cache entries, and compile only missing or invalid items.

## Implementation and bounded validation

Source 0.4.17 adds a validated sequential startup bundle and identity-keyed deterministic compiler-failure cache. The original installation was backed up and updated in place only for its EXE, source-version file, and local-runtime-update manifest; this is not a complete release package.

The original v0.4.16 installation audit found 22,972 valid compiled binaries and two repeated DXC failures, not a mass recompilation. Two D3D12 `--prepare-shaders-only` starts against the same original cache exited normally before guest startup. The first migration initialized in 10.781 s and made two actual DXC attempts/rejections. The second initialized in 3.634 s: 77 ms metadata snapshot, 2,397 ms bundle load, 22,972 modules ready, two cached failures, zero source-content reads, translations, or process-wide actual DXC calls, and 288 ready PSOs in 18 ms. Five protected user files and existing cache metadata remained unchanged; only the first run added the bundle and two `.failed` records, and the second added nothing.

The unified Release build exited 0 and the new `LoShaderStartupCacheTest` passed. This demonstrates consecutive preparation-only reuse in one original-installation D3D12 cache. It does not claim either retained compiler error was repaired, Vulkan or gameplay coverage, other platforms, a full release, or player acceptance. QOL7's logical-thread-minus-one worker evidence remains separate.

Evidence: `out/v0.5.0/shader-startup-recurrence/deployment.json`, `out/v0.5.0/shader-startup-recurrence/startup-1/result.json`, `out/v0.5.0/shader-startup-recurrence/startup-2/result.json`, `out/v0.5.0/shader-startup-recurrence/validation-summary.json`, `out/v0.5.0/shader-startup-recurrence/REPORT.md`.

items.title: Profile steady-state CPU hotspots on Windows
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:steady-state-cpu-hotspot-profile -->

Profile the steady-state Windows CPU cost before proposing an optimization.

## Validation and limits

The actual v0.4.15 D3D12 Map2 profile used the fixed native save point, 60 FPS cap, SMAA, 720p internal and configured 1080p output on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D (16 logical processors) with an RTX 5080. Across 45.0001416 seconds, the process used 110.875 CPU seconds (15.3993% whole-machine CPU; 2.46388 logical-core equivalents). ETW recorded 112,344 on-CPU samples, zero lost events, and 20 missing stacks.

The two CPU-heavy threads account for 80.3833% of process CPU time: the thread carrying guest GPU-query polling used 44.78125 CPU seconds (40.389%), and the thread carrying zero-timeout guest shared-value polling used 44.34375 CPU seconds (39.994%). Those values are thread CPU-time shares, not a claim that every cycle is in either polling path. The measured query-poll path `sub_823CE960` → `sub_823CF390` → `sub_823CF3F0` has 41,075 on-CPU samples (36.5618% of process samples; 91.3509% of its thread samples). The measured shared-value path `sub_82322478` → `sub_827CACA8` → zero-timeout `KeDelayExecutionThread` has 37,180 on-CPU samples (33.0948% of process samples; 83.0244% of its thread samples); the two paths total 69.6566% of process samples. These inclusive path shares are sample distributions, not CPU-time accounting. GPU WorkerMain used 17.921875 CPU seconds (16.164%); `getenv_nolock` is 24.6787% of that GPU thread's exclusive on-CPU samples even with capture disabled.

This is a single D3D12 scene profile, not whole-game coverage, a temperature diagnosis, or a backend regression conclusion. System/driver attribution remains unresolved. GPU-query waiting, zero-timeout polling, and per-draw environment lookups were candidates identified during profiling; their subsequent implementation is recorded by the separate optimization item. The completed profiling itself did not implement or validate those changes.

Evidence: `out/v0.5.0/cpu-hotspots/report-summary.json`; `out/v0.5.0/cpu-hotspots/REPORT.md`; `out/v0.5.0/cpu-hotspots/report/HOTSPOTS.html`; `out/v0.5.0/cpu-comparison/report/REPORT.html`.

items.title: [Bug] kalm daughter funreal pick up flower
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:issue12-kalm-daughter-funeral-flower-crash -->

Open Issue #12 is a **P1 narrative-progression repair awaiting current production validation**. The reporter says the game crashes on an MSI Claw A1M after collecting all ten flowers at Kaim's daughter funeral and talking to a character. They identify their build only as “latest recomp”; the report initially lacked an exact version, backend, logs, save, stack trace, and attachment. The reporter has since supplied a save attachment, and the local reproduction captured a runtime crash log; neither supplies a resolved host stack or identifies the reported executable/backend. The report also says Disc 2's final boss was playable, which is context only and does not establish a cause or coverage boundary.

## Triage scope and completion criteria

- [x] Locate the reported story context in offline game text: `nbr_1`/`nbv_1` share the ten-white-flower hand-in to Melvi; `nbv_1` row 13 is the flower-completion line; current `name_data.xml` identifies Map108 as Ghost Town — City of Ruins and Map109 as Ghost Town — Funeral Beach
- [ ] Establish whether candidate events `RT_072C`/`RT_073C` execute from that hand-in; their link is not yet proven
- [x] Review the selected PPC-to-generated-C++ dispatch slice: seven functions / 422 instructions reviewed, with no root cause found; this is not a complete root-cause audit
- [x] Create isolated native pre-hand-in and 10/10 saves, then trigger the story on the exact official executable in a background, muted run; original data preserved
- [x] Capture the crash contract: runtime log, native save provenance, guest `CTR=0` and `LR=823CB53C`; no host-resolved stack is available
- [x] Establish the captured failure path: GC frees old MaterialInstanceConstant objects while the previous frame still draws an old skeletal-mesh proxy (run09/10 and run13)
- [x] Implement and locally merge pre-GC / pending-purge rendering drains; reuse same-source diagnostic run14 and bounded code review
- [ ] Complete current production-build validation, natural-timing hand-in and directly affected performance coverage; then apply one development patch increment

## Current evidence and acceptance

Offline text extraction narrows the story context but does not establish an executed event link or root cause: `nbr_1`/`nbv_1` share the ten-white-flower delivery to Melvi, `nbv_1` row 13 records completion, while later rows 66–67 concern torch/branch preparation. Current `name_data.xml` directly identifies Map108/109 as the City of Ruins and Funeral Beach maps, not an established font/display-index defect; `RT_072C`/`RT_073C` remain candidate events only.

The crash is now locally reproduced on the official v0.4.2 executable (SHA256 `13f1294bbb54efbf9a712a066441cb019ba5497cf1242bde6905e6c8bc1757b6`). From a native generated 0/10 save that independently loaded, the controlled path collected all ten flowers through normal A input, used the original 109→108→109 exit route, and used same-map coordinate assistance only for location (no counter or completion-flag writes). The native 10/10 save completed successfully; after Melvi's “Ah, you've gathered the flowers...” dialogue, one normal A input reproduced an execute access violation (`guestCTR=0`, `LR=823CB53C`). The run did not use Cheat Engine 2× speed.

Run04 independently loaded the native 10/10 save and captured the first invalid-object state after the Melvi hand-in. Nine read-only debugger context/base/LR/CTR checks passed. `r3` began at `03B6A480` with first word `03B6A560`, then advanced to `03B6A640` in `0xE0` steps; word 2 is `1` and `+0x124` is `0`. The original allocator free branch at `0x82298A1C` writes `[block+4]=1`, links `[block]=[pool+16]`, then stores the block at `[pool+16]`, matching the observed free-list format. This points the execute-null path at an invalid/freed-object representation rather than proving a static vtable-method omission. At the run04 checkpoint, the actual free/write moment had not yet been captured; that historical evidence alone did not establish a specific UAF owner or repair. The later run09-14 evidence below supersedes that diagnostic limit. Runtime evidence: `out/issue12-triage/runtime/run-03/runtime.log`; targeted analysis: `out/issue12-triage/translation/crash-analysis/REPORT.md`.

On 2026-09-09, Claude's later run09/10 official v0.4.2 captures identified old MIC ownership and free flags; run13 observed GC reclaiming the old materials before a delayed render proxy used them (five stale-draw hits). Run14 used the same fix source and forced delay: preflush removed the old proxy before collection, with zero stale draws and no crash. This diagnostic build used an external hook chain, excluded poll_wait and enabled SKIP_STALE; zero stale hits means the skip guard did not fire. It does not establish current uninstrumented production behavior or broad gameplay/performance acceptance.

The source repair from `17e3ab7` is now locally merged from `claude-issue12` into `0.5.0` at `9cefb0d`. ABI, strong-symbol dispatch registration, CMake inclusion and same-source artifact evidence passed read-only review; no merge-only build or test was repeated. Current production build, natural-timing hand-in and directly affected performance validation remain pending. Source stays `0.4.18` until proportionate validation is complete; target remains **v0.5.0**. No push, tag, release or GC-patch player acceptance is claimed. The current [root-cause report](docs/notes/issue12-root-cause.md) and [Claude handoff](docs/notes/issue12-handoff-2026-09-09.md) supersede the earlier run08 recovery checkpoint.

The Issue remains open. In the 2026-09-09T04:25:46Z comment, the reporter says turning off speedhack and possibly avoiding cutscene skipping resolved the separate torch-flame symptom and they reached Disc 1's final dungeon. This workaround has not been independently validated and is not acceptance of this GC repair.

items.title: Investigate remaining stalls and shader-startup compiler failures
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:performance-and-shader-startup -->

Investigate city CPU stalls and the two retained shader-startup compiler failures. Do not generalize a fixed Hidden-city measurement to the full game.

## Completed bounded city segment — 2026-09-12

Stage timing diagnosed the 41.8241 ms vertex insertion spike as `std::unordered_map` rehash/growth (262,144→524,288 buckets), rather than endian copying: all 495 copies totalled 0.0254 ms at that hitch. `gpu/vertex_cache.h` now uses a 65,536-entry reserved bounded dense metadata cache and evicts the least-recently-used item from at most 16 rotating candidates before insertion. This retains the existing quality, 1280×720 D3D12 AA=3, two-slot and arena/wait policy: no `kGpuSlots`, `WaitForGpu` wrapping or item-1 rollback.

`LoVertexCacheTest` passed once with 3,569,548 checks. It establishes metadata ownership/replacement/eviction behavior without creating a GPU device or running the game. Final runtime evidence uses the same EXE as the preceding bounded-cache run, moving only driver input and screenshot-request files to TEMP. The observed stable post-present maximum fell from 412.9283 to 0.4193 ms; this localizes measurement-path I/O but does not establish a filesystem or scheduler cause.

## Result and boundary

The final Hidden route has 1,790 city frames, 59.651463 mean FPS, and a 1600–2800 fixed window of 1,201 frames at 59.918376 mean FPS, 54.494611 1% low, 50.374688% accepted presents above 16.67 ms, 22.5913 ms maximum present, 2.2981 ms maximum vertex, zero rehashes, and zero stable-window draws above budget. The requested mean threshold of at least 58 FPS is met under the 60 FPS cap. All-city 1% low remains 45.989346 FPS and maximum present is 43.0117 ms due to the retained city-entry bind/load tail.

This is bounded near-60 city evidence, not an every-frame 60 FPS lock, strict S4 pass, whole-game result, player acceptance or release. Original saves were unchanged in every run and before/after inventories; final local unpublished EXE SHA-256 is `9D9460248FEB72AC7239ABD40AC1DA6619847F176CF4AA38AD6F725C6923852B`.

## Historical CPU candidates — 2026-09-13

Prior WPR identified `SampledContent::Visit<Matches>` at 2,474 self (23.4147%) / 2,729 inclusive (25.8281%) of 10,566 ordinary render samples. `EqualSampleBlock64` passed 33,927 focused checks on Clang 19.1.5 and 22.1.8. The fixed-40-W/user00/internal-4K baseline-to-SIMD comparison was 46.787 to 47.074 FPS (+0.61%) while GPU queue was 20.782 to 20.661 ms; the same executable's 1080p diagnostic was 59.981 FPS / 5.843-ms GPU queue, not a setting recommendation. WPR TID 26308 attributed 450/4,393 self samples (10.2436%) to repeated `LO_QUERY_TRACE` environment lookup; the presence cache preserves hook order and diagnostics. A combined local dirty candidate SHA-256 `10fc929307e293d6169d858ef974c7cccc2f09831391ae0ef6b46fe9e0bbb711` built in 33.818s, and one 40-W new-vs-SIMD window was 47.073714 to 47.088493 FPS with CPU -1.37% and essentially unchanged render CPU/GPU queue. The matching PPC-library identity and original-EXE/save preservation apply to these historical SIMD/combined-candidate comparisons only. They do not establish stable benefit, 60 FPS, player acceptance, or an identity claim for the later installed v0.5.8 package.

## Historical pre-v0.5.9 recomp-depth diagnosis — 2026-09-13

The installed v0.5.8 package (`6e6f11c`; runtime SHA-256 `89f1ec23…106d`) was observed at user-set 40 W/internal 4K. Its lossless WPR maps render TID 42136 to 41.86% of ordinary on-CPU samples and high-CPU guest rendering TID 43848 uniquely to `RenderingThreadMain`; no busy-spin primary-cause evidence was found. A 4.3-ms read-only texture-cache snapshot found 386 items in 512 buckets, only 33 nonempty buckets and a longest chain of 84. All guest addresses were 4-KiB aligned, so current address low bits lose entropy in bucket selection. This is an earlier diagnostic checkpoint: texture-hash finalization has since been implemented in `texture_key.h`, and `LoTextureKeyTest` passed 54,877 checks once. The independent performance benefit of that hash change is not yet established; default-occlusion pseudo-visible draws remain source-confirmed but unquantified. The diagnosis still has no A/B, 60-FPS proof, player acceptance, commit or release; these statements concern the diagnosis and its candidates, not the already installed v0.5.8 package.

## Historical pre-v0.5.9 implementation state — 2026-09-13

The user authorized an optimization turn toward Vulkan 1080p60 at 15 W. Implementation has started on the texture-hash correction and a correctness-preserving per-draw CPU reduction. The initial controlled comparison remains internal 4K at 60 W with the existing bench scripts on checkout source 0.5.7; installed v0.5.8 remains separate diagnostic provenance. No controlled result is available yet. The 15-W/1080p60 goal is a target, not a commitment or achieved performance. No commit, push, release, version change or player acceptance is authorized or recorded for this turn.

The user reports that the previous release performs normally, without an FPS, power, 1080p or 15-W acceptance value. The release baseline remains intentionally unrun; investigation resumed at the user's direction. Work continues on the identified Vulkan per-draw descriptor/constant submission optimization, with testing limited to the specific change or unresolved question. The verified installed/published release is v0.5.8 (published 2026-09-13T15:11:11Z; EXE SHA-256 `89f1ec23c3d6a7c16b9f7fc8f66e38a3059cc90132cf80f071eb671322ac106d`). The hash/shader-identity changes and focused fixture remain uncommitted; unverified descriptor/push/GPU-probe experiments were moved to `out` and removed from source. The Vulkan 1080p60-at-15-W goal remains unaccepted.

A Vulkan-only depth-clear coalescing repair combines the 720 fragmented rectangles into one exact-coverage clear. In the static copied user01 view at internal 4K/60 W, paired 45-second windows improved from 7.49638 to 43.47614 FPS; GPU time fell from 132.91221 to 21.06364 ms, record time from 37.30861 to 4.93429 ms, and process CPU from 75.25888 to 41.74892 ms/frame. Control SHA-256 `1b9c3c01b1a6863cedb91050c9bc09f77b3ed04f697409c99ea8a72948015ef3` and candidate `bca61967e96fbcb2017118cb1c0136ec980770bd6a112ef521d9727cf5653a5f` are source 0.5.7 at `1c93c397af7bbeb240feabf90d895f9dfdac8a9c` plus dirty worktree, uncommitted and unpublished. The CPU coalescer (1,501,504 pixels/9 MSAA pairs) and two 3840×2208 Vulkan GPU fixtures (zero pixel difference; bottom 48 rows retained) passed once. No 1080p/15-W result, post-repair player acceptance, commit or release is recorded; 4K also remains below 60 FPS. The user said v0.5.8 D3D12 was about 38.5 FPS and later reported Vulkan menu stutter, so no Vulkan-release-normal claim applies. Evidence: `out/vulkan-perf-20260913/clear-coalesce-comparison.json`.

## Historical pre-v0.5.9 Vulkan binding candidate — 2026-09-13

A conservative Vulkan graphics descriptor-binding suppression is implemented in dirty source 0.5.7 at `47a9cd4d5d1d49cb1db000eaf711f6827a53cdeb`; `LostOdysseyRecomp-bind-only.exe` SHA-256 `85a2c81d3a63a243acb82abdf3708ef723122ba6b24e25a0906a5c8156116256` exists only under `out`. The focused binding-cache test passed 32 pixels / 128 components, incompatible-layout A/B/A and fence reuse. Against the reused clear-coalesce control in one fixed copied-save, internal-4K/Vulkan/AA3/60-cap/60-W 45-second window, bind-only was 43.01324 versus 43.47614 FPS, record 4.75117 versus 4.93429 ms, GPU 21.17160 versus 21.06364 ms, and aggregate process CPU 44.16216 versus 41.74892 ms/frame; sensor GPU clocks were 2519.24 versus 2557.05 MHz. It establishes no overall FPS or total-CPU gain. A constants-SIMD experiment regressed cost and was reverted, retained only in `out`. The native city probe’s 4.40584-ms group 578 spans four draws with scene copy, TAA and intervening work, so it is not an isolated TAA cost. The installed earlier candidate and launcher are unchanged. No commit, push, release, 1080p/15-W result or player acceptance is recorded. items.title: Fix Vulkan pixel-shader LoopEnd predicate exit
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:vulkan-ps-loopend-predicate-exit -->

Correct the Xenos pixel-shader LoopEnd translation when its predicate ends a loop. Preserve Xbox 64-lane exit semantics and add regression coverage for related shaders.

## Diagnosis evidence

Release v0.5.6, Vulkan, RTX 5080, 3840x2160 capture frame 12462: PS `a195c4db25859691` has a CF LoopEnd whose predicate break is missing from translation. The loop executes 255 iterations although at most eight are effective, producing empty work. The recompiled baseline matched the captured SPIR-V; a one-line offline shader-only probe with `if (!p0) break` produced a byte-identical final PNG. After all games exited, ABBA means fell from 7.711424 to 1.244464 ms for affected shadow draws (83.9%) and from 14.026832 to 7.1088 ms for all timed events (49.3%).

## Limits

This is a single-frame local diagnosis and offline probe, not a production translator fix, regression pass, game validation, player acceptance or release. It does not establish FPS or power change.

items.title: [Bug] Numara Castle has inverted lights
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:issue-38-numara-castle-inverted-lights -->

Issue #38 reports inverted/black lights ("anti-lights emitting darkness") in Numara Castle (Philosopher's Chamber).

## Root cause and repair

- Root cause: The Xenos translator shader epilogue clamped unsigned 7e3 EDRAM format (`COLOR_2_10_10_10_FLOAT`) to `[-31.875, 31.875]`. Additive light blending wrote negative light values to the host EDRAM target, causing subsequent tone-mapping `log2` to produce NaNs and pitch black voids.
- Repair: In `LostOdysseyRecomp/gpu/renderer.cpp` and `LostOdysseyRecomp/gpu/shader/xenos_translator.cpp`, enforced a strict `0.0` lower bound for unsigned EDRAM formats (formats 0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 12). Bumped shader cache `Version` from 22 to 23 in `LostOdysseyRecomp/gpu/shader/cache.h` to invalidate stale cached DXIL binaries.

## Recorded validation

- Verification confirmed black diamond voids eliminated and lantern lighting and bloom cleanly restored in Philosopher's Chamber.
- Test suite passing (`LoTemporalJitterTest`, `LoMenuRenderTest`).

## Status and delivery boundary

Fixed in commit `7484518` on branch `menu`, merged via PR #43 and published in release `v0.5.20`. Issue #38 closed with release and commit reference.

items.title: Portable Vulkan shader pack (.lospv)
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:portable-vulkan-shader-pack -->

Implement relocatable, self-contained Vulkan shader pack (.lospv) with Zstandard compression for instant startup without first-run compilation.

## Implementation and validation

- Relocatable `.lospv` container format encapsulating 28,482 SPIR-V shaders and TranslatedShader metadata without raw HLSL, debug logs, or build failures.
- SHA-256 bytecode deduplication and Zstandard chunked block compression (~1 MiB blocks) compressing bundle to 169.9 MB.
- Runtime lazy loading and memory-mapped block decoding eliminates first-run compilation on Vulkan (WSL2 Linux verified 1.2s zero-compile startup with 0 DXC calls).
- Fully decoupled from host filesystem paths and host DXC DLL identities for cross-platform reuse (Windows/Linux/Steam Deck, x86-64/ARM64).
- Bundled automatically into Windows x64 ZIP and Linux x64 AppImage release archives via `tools/release/fetch_shader_pack.py` and published as standalone release asset in v0.5.20.

items.title: Optimize shader and pipeline preparation throughput and options
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:shader-preparation-optimization -->

Scale worker concurrency by host resources, prioritize main game shaders, and support interactive skip and persistence.

## Implementation and validation

- Worker scaling by host resources: hosts with >= 8 GB physical RAM use `logicalThreads - 1` concurrency; hosts with < 8 GB retain a safe 4-worker limit to prevent OOM.
- Added `LO_SHADER_WORKERS` and `LO_PIPELINE_WORKERS` environment variables for explicit concurrency tuning.
- Removed Windows `MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH` synchronous flush flag on disk cache writes, relying on OS write caching to eliminate small-file disk seek stalls.
- Priority prebuilding: primary XEX and core game shaders (priority 0) compile first, predictive variants (priority 1) follow.
- Interactive and configured skip: pressing ESC, Space, or gamepad B safely skips remaining startup prebuild while persisting already-compiled shaders. Added `skip_shader_prebuild` in `settings.ini`.

Provide dedicated incremental build scripts for Linux ELF compilation on native Linux and under Windows WSL2.

## Implementation and validation

- Added `tools/build_linux.sh` for native Linux incremental builds with automatic dependency discovery.
- Added `tools/build_wsl.bat` for launching WSL2 Linux builds directly from Windows development environments.
- Integrated portable shader pack packaging (`tools/release/package_shader_bundle.py`) into automated build and release staging.
- Verified on WSL2 Manjaro with clang 18 and CMake Ninja generators.

## Sources

- https://github.com/freefrank/LostOdysseyRecomp/releases/tag/v0.5.20
- https://github.com/freefrank/LostOdysseyRecomp/commit/6081fcc
- `tools/build_linux.sh`
- `tools/build_wsl.bat`
- `tools/release/package_shader_bundle.py`

items.title: Fix D3D12 motion replay PSO creation failure E_INVALIDARG
items.body:
<!-- lo-project:d3d12-motion-replay-pso-invalidarg -->

## Background and failure mode

In automated validation of the geometric motion replay pipeline under Direct3D 12, asynchronously generated replay shaders compile cleanly (DXIL jobs complete successfully). However, the D3D12 replay PSO creation call (`CreateGraphicsPipelineState`) returns `E_INVALIDARG` (`0x80070057`). Runtime execution repeatedly logs `MV pipeline allocation failed`, resulting in `replay=0 ready=false consume=false`.

Validation run reference: `runtime-639254046562050769.log`.

The Vulkan backend implementation succeeds in the same scene and achieves `replay>0 ready=true consume=true`. This task is scoped strictly to the D3D12 backend.

## Acceptance criteria

- Identify the exact invalid field or state incompatibility in the D3D12 `CreateGraphicsPipelineState` descriptor (e.g., shader bytecode, root signature, input layout, rasterizer, blend, or depth/stencil state) within `motion_replay_gpu.h` / `plume_d3d12.cpp`.
- D3D12 replay PSO creates successfully without returning `E_INVALIDARG`.
- Automated test scene achieves `replay>0`, `ready=true`, and `consume=true` under D3D12.
- No regression on the working Vulkan path.

## Sources

- Validation run: `runtime-639254046562050769.log`
- `LostOdysseyRecomp/gpu/motion_replay_gpu.h`
- `thirdparty/plume/plume_d3d12.cpp`
- `docs/notes/motion-vector-implementation.md`

fields.Evidence: Observed in automated validation log runtime-639254046562050769.log: DXIL replay shaders compile successfully, but D3D12 CreateGraphicsPipelineState fails with E_INVALIDARG 0x80070057 ('MV pipeline allocation failed'), yielding replay=0 ready=false consume=false. Vulkan path passes (replay>0 ready=true consume=true). Scoped to D3D12 backend repair.
